claims.reason: Both zigzag theorems end with the same homotopical argument, from `have := kq.twoOutOfThree` to `MorphismProperty.of_retract hr hvW`. The steps are: set up the `ContainsIdentities` and `IsStableUnderRetracts` instances; use `cylinder_weakEquivalence_iff` with `endpoint false ≫ U = 𝟙` to show `endpoint true ≫ U` is a weak equivalence; transfer along `huv` to `V` and rewrite with `hv₀` to get `p ≫ j` weak; then build the `RetractArrow j (p ≫ j)` from `j ≫ p = 𝟙` and apply `of_retract`. The finite version runs the same tail on `Y.val`, `jb`, `pb`, with `hjp' : jb ≫ pb = 𝟙 X.val`. `glue_finite_stationary_cylinder` yields `U V : G.cylinder.obj Y.val ⟶ Y.val`, and `Y.val` is a `StrictOmegaCategory.{0}`. So the tail uses only `hjp`, `hu₀`, `huv`, `hv₀`, `aw`, `kq`. It uses neither the pushout, nor the truncation input `t`, nor any dimension bound. The lemma therefore needs no extra assumptions and adds no import cycle; `cylinder_weakEquivalence_iff` comes from the already-imported TopologicalConePrism. The argument (homotopy invariance, then 2-out-of-3, then retract) is about 20 lines of real reasoning. The same pattern appears elsewhere, for example in `deformation_retract_weakEquivalences` in TopologicalConePrism. The shared lemma has a clear meaning, and each theorem would keep only its pushout-specific `hom_ext` computations. One placement caveat: the lemma needs its own section, with variables `G aw kq` only (no `t`), placed before the finite theorem.
claims.shared_lemma: theorem weakEquivalence_of_two_cylinder_retract {X Y : StrictOmegaCategory.{0}} (j : X ⟶ Y) (p : Y ⟶ X) (hjp : j ≫ p = 𝟙 X) (U V : G.cylinder.obj Y ⟶ Y) (hu₀ : (G.endpoint false).app Y ≫ U = 𝟙 Y) (huv : (G.endpoint true).app Y ≫ U = (G.endpoint true).app Y ≫ V) (hv₀ : (G.endpoint false).app Y ≫ V = p ≫ j) : h.streetWeakEquivalences j  -- with variables {h} (G : RightGrayInput h) (aw) (kq) and `include aw kq`. Proof: the current lines 223–241 of the infinite version, unchanged.
